title: The Boy Scout Who Built A Nuclear Reactor In His Shed
sources: Harper's Magazine / Ken Silverstein 'The Radioactive Boy Scout' (1998) - In 1994, 17-year-old David Hahn built a makeshift nuclear breeder reactor in Commerce Township, Michigan.
EPA Superfund / NRC records - In August 1994, federal authorities discovered the shed emitted radiation 1,000 times normal background levels, resulting in a Superfund cleanup of 39 sealed barrels.

lines.text: In nineteen ninety-four, federal agents in hazmat suits raided a teenager's backyard potting shed -

lines.text: and discovered a working radioactive breeder reactor.
Seventeen-year-old David Hahn wanted to earn the Boy Scout atomic energy merit badge.
Instead of just reading pamphlets, he decided to build an actual nuclear reactor in his mom's garden shed.
David posed as a physics teacher to extract government research,
then bought hundreds of smoke detectors to harvest radioactive americium.
He scraped thorium off camping lantern mantles and bought radium clocks from antique shops.
Using lead blocks, duct tape, and a tin-foil core, his makeshift reactor started generating lethal radiation.
When his homemade Geiger counter went berserk five blocks away, David panicked and packed the core into his car trunk.
Police pulled him over, searched the trunk, and instantly called the FBI.
Federal emergency teams dismantled the shed, sealed it into thirty-nine barrels, and buried it in the Utah desert.
David still earned his Boy Scout badge, but left the entire neighborhood contaminated.
